A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RCE-KD research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original recommendation experiments, training-cost measurements, ablations, sensitivity analyses and sequential recommendation results in Section 6 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds scheduling studies, training-dynamics analyses, SASRec results and multimodal recommendation experiments.

M1.justification: The item partition, sampling distribution, two CE losses and exponential overlap-based weighting in Equations 7–11 remain unchanged. The scheduling alternatives are experimental controls, and the additional applications use the existing distillation procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix D.2 adds Netflix, Tiktok and Amazon Electronics evaluations with visual, textual and, for Tiktok, acoustic information in teacher inputs. This substantially extends domains and modalities beyond the retained CiteULike, Gowalla and Yelp tasks. SASRec expands configurations within already existing sequential coverage.

E2.justification: TARec is added to the main and sequential performance comparisons. Full-item CE is added to the ablations. The new multimodal comparison evaluates HetComp, PromptMM and TARec, explicitly disabling embedding-level distillation in the latter two. TARec is excluded from the training-efficiency comparison.

E3.justification: V2 adds training-set NDCG@10 monitoring, controlled scheduling comparisons, SASRec teacher/student configurations, and BM3-to-MF/LightGCN evaluations with restricted multimodal baselines. These substantially extend the evaluation design. Existing chronological splits, sequential holdouts, ranking metrics and original backbone configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds training-dynamics comparisons against vanilla CE. Appendix C.5 tests increasing versus decreasing weights, global versus user-specific schedules, and linear versus exponential schedules, supported by overlap trajectories and histograms. Full-item CE also extends the existing ablations; prior overlap and hyperparameter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five independent runs, paired t-tests with a 0.05 threshold, and standard deviations for ablation and hyperparameter plots. The new multimodal performance table follows the existing testing practice. Changed p-values do not establish a changed statistical procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial TARec, full-CE, scheduling, SASRec and multimodal results. Existing performance scores in Table 1 and v1 Table 8/v2 Table 12 are retained, while some baseline-relative improvements and p-values change. For example, Yelp LightGCN-to-LightGCN NDCG@10 improvement becomes 7.36% instead of 8.20% after adding TARec. Some new entries are inconsistent with the stated rankings, notably TARec's printed CiteULike Recall@20 of 0.370 in Table 1.

T1.justification: Appendix C.5.1 adds a gradient-norm contribution formula and a derivative-sign argument linking decreasing gamma to greater L1 influence. The central CE–NDCG theorems, closure assumption, partial-NDCG definition and Appendix B proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about the closure-conditioned CE–NDCG connection, RCE-KD's split-and-fusion design, and effective, efficient distillation. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands the explanation of scheduling through user-specific learning progress and the claimed necessity of exponential weighting. It also interprets higher training NDCG as evidence of tighter bounds, attributes performance relative to full-CE to bound tightness, and extends applicability arguments to multimodal teachers. These interpretations go beyond v1's existing explanations.

D1.justification: V2 supplements the retained implementation recipe with SASRec block/head counts, multimodal feature encoders and dimensions, dataset statistics, and BM3/student dimensions in Tables 11, 13 and 14. The code-access pointer changes from anonymous hosting to a named GitHub repository; accessibility cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for TARec, SASRec, multimodal datasets, BM3, PromptMM and feature encoders, with a local comparison of logit-only and embedding-level distillation in Appendix D.2. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative receives limited grammatical and citation-format edits, updated affiliations and publication headers, and acknowledgments. Appendix A becomes a visualization section, and sequential experiments move from C.5 to D.1. The established exposition is largely retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds training curves, overlap trajectories, histograms, scheduling tables and multimodal tables. Figure 1 gains RCE-KD bars, ablation figures gain full-CE bars, and performance tables expand with TARec rows and a SASRec block. These materially expand the displays; existing ranking and hyperparameter plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The added full-CE and scheduling controls, stronger comparator coverage, and SASRec/multimodal evaluations improve scrutiny and empirical support for the unchanged method. The gain is tempered by new numerical inconsistencies, including Table 1's TARec value of 0.370, and Appendix A.2's unsupported inference that higher training NDCG establishes tighter mathematical bounds. The revision provides useful additional evidence, but its interpretation and reporting limit the overall improvement.
